attempts.summary: Created an opsbot account on node1 and node2 and configured SSH key-based access from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 using Ansible run from node1. Installed Ansible 2.9.27 on node1 (had to add EPEL + CentOS 7.9 vault base/updates/extras repos since no yum repos were enabled and the standard EPEL mirror is retired). The playbook (~/ansible/opsbot/site.yml on node1) creates opsbot with a locked password on both hosts, generates an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installs its public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and appends a 'Match User opsbot' sshd block (PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) on both node1 and node2, then restarts sshd. Verified opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH works via key and that password/non-pubkey auth is rejected for opsbot on both nodes. All three managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) were then restarted one at a time via systemctl reboot, with boot_id captured before/after to prove an actual restart occurred, and opsbot/sshd functionality was re-verified as healthy after each restart before moving to the next node.
